description: WILDFIRE: GLOBAL INFERNO — Where Nature's Fury Meets Global Strategy. Explore the science of wildfire propagation through an interactive 2D world map. Experience how wind, temperature, humidity and vegetation shape the spread of devastating fires. Track affected nations, simulate global impacts, and discover the delicate balance between environmental forces and human resilience. One World. One Fire. Countless Consequences.

details:
Project Details — WILDFIRE: GLOBAL INFERNO

What does it do and how does it work?

Wildfire: Global Inferno is an interactive, browser-based global wildfire simulation that combines geographical visualisation, environmental modelling and strategy-based gameplay. It uses a detailed 2D world map with country boundaries to demonstrate how wildfires can spread across different geographical regions.

The simulation considers environmental factors such as temperature, humidity, wind direction, rainfall and vegetation to influence fire propagation. Users can evolve their wildfire through upgrades, while countries respond with countermeasures. A live dashboard tracks affected and unaffected countries, simulated casualties and overall wildfire progression.

What benefits does it have?

The project transforms complex environmental concepts into an accessible and engaging experience. It helps users understand how environmental conditions influence wildfire behaviour, how geographical differences affect vulnerability, and why controlling wildfires can become increasingly challenging.

What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to encourage environmental awareness and improve public understanding of wildfire dynamics and disaster preparedness. By making wildfire behaviour interactive, we hope to inspire curiosity about Earth science, environmental protection and the importance of effective disaster management.

What tools and technologies were used?

The project was developed as a browser-based application using HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript. JavaScript handles the simulation logic, environmental variables, country statistics and interactive gameplay, while HTML and CSS provide the interface and visual presentation. Geographical data is used to represent country boundaries and create the global map. Development and testing were carried out using Visual Studio Code and a local browser environment.

How is the project creative?

Instead of presenting wildfire information through static maps and statistics, we created an interactive global simulation that allows users to explore wildfire propagation and its potential consequences. The combination of a geographical world map, evolving fire mechanics, country-level statistics and simulated global casualties creates an engaging approach to environmental education.

What factors did our team consider?

We considered geographical accuracy, environmental variability, simulation performance, accessibility and ease of use. We also focused on distinguishing simulated outcomes from real-world observations, ensuring that estimated casualties and wildfire progression are understood as illustrative rather than scientifically validated predictions.

Our vision: One World. One Fire. Countless Consequences.
